provenance: Original synthetic fixtures authored for Code Steward Agent; not executed during creation.

rubric.purpose: Validate input as IP address literals and print only valid IPv4 addresses.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Reads stdin lines, skips parse failures and IPv6, and prints the accepted addresses.
rubric.evidence: Lines 6, 7, 9, 10: ip_address parses the text and the version comparison filters IPv4.
rubric.unknowns: Actual addresses/counts are unknown; accepting syntax does not establish reachability or safety.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim DNS lookup, ping, geolocation, network scanning or live connectivity checks.

rubric.purpose: Read service settings from an INI file and print a host:port description.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Reads service.ini; requires a service section and host; uses port 8080 if that key is absent, then prints.
rubric.dependencies: Standard library configparser; external service.ini is referenced but not supplied.
rubric.evidence: Lines 4, 5, 6, 7: Section/key reads supply host and port; getint sets the fallback; print emits the description.
rubric.unknowns: Actual host and config contents are unknown; missing section/host can fail despite the port fallback.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim the program connects to the host, starts a service or defaults every missing setting.

rubric.purpose: Parse supplied HTML and print href values on anchor start tags.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Reads HTML from stdin; prints each encountered anchor href value.
rubric.evidence: Lines 5, 6, 8, 11: handle_starttag selects a tags and href attributes; feed receives stdin text.
rubric.unknowns: Actual HTML/links are unknown; href values are not validated or resolved against a base URL.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim this downloads web pages, follows links, deduplicates URLs or checks link health.

rubric.purpose: Generate three synthetic rows with IDs and seeded pseudorandom integer values, printed as CSV.
rubric.inputs_outputs: No external data input is shown; writes a header and three rows to stdout, with IDs 0..2 and values 1..10 inclusive.
rubric.dependencies: Standard library csv, random and sys; Random(7) is a local seeded generator.
rubric.evidence: Lines 5, 7, 8, 9: The fixed seed, range(3) and randint bounds define generation and CSV output.
rubric.unknowns: Exact generated values need verification for the intended runtime; no real-world data source or business meaning is supplied.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not call the numbers cryptographically secure, invent measured data, or assert a named output file.

rubric.purpose: Print the median of numeric command-line arguments.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Converts arguments after the script name to floats; outputs their median to stdout.
rubric.evidence: Lines 4, 5: The argument conversion and median call distinguish this from computing a mean.
rubric.unknowns: Actual values/result are unknown; an empty list or nonnumeric argument can fail.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not describe arithmetic mean, CSV input or automatic handling of invalid/empty input.

rubric.purpose: Parse a command-line ISO-format timestamp and print an ISO-format UTC conversion.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Reads the first CLI argument; emits a converted timestamp string to stdout.
rubric.evidence: Lines 4, 5: fromisoformat parses and astimezone(timezone.utc) performs the conversion.
rubric.unknowns: Actual input is unknown. An offset-free/naive input is interpreted using local timezone behavior, so environment matters.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not assume every input includes a timezone or that an offset-free time is already UTC; do not invent the resulting timestamp.

rubric.purpose: Export an asynchronous function that fetches a caller-provided URL and returns response status information.
rubric.inputs_outputs: check receives a URL; when called it performs a request and resolves to status/ok fields. No call is shown.
rubric.dependencies: A runtime with fetch and CommonJS module.exports support; no imported third-party package is shown.
rubric.evidence: Lines 2, 3, 5: The fetch call and returned status/ok object specify behavior; module.exports exposes the function.
rubric.unknowns: Actual URL, response, runtime support and error outcomes are unknown; no response body is consumed here.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim it parses JSON, retries, checks a particular website or made a request during static analysis.

rubric.purpose: Define a TypeScript function selecting IDs of users whose enabled field is true.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Receives a typed User array and returns a string array of selected IDs; does not mutate the input array in this expression.
rubric.dependencies: TypeScript and array filter/map; no imported packages.
rubric.evidence: Lines 1, 3, 4: The type describes fields; the implemented filter/map expression defines runtime selection and projection.
rubric.unknowns: Actual user records and caller are unknown; static types do not implement validation of arbitrary runtime input.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim database access, user authentication, sorting, deduplication or comprehensive runtime schema validation.

rubric.purpose: List paths matching immediate regular .log files under the first argument directory.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Takes a directory argument; prints each matched regular-file path, one per line.
rubric.dependencies: sh-compatible shell with glob expansion, file test and printf.
rubric.evidence: Lines 2, 3, 4: The glob selects immediate matches, -f skips non-files/unmatched literal patterns, and printf prints paths.
rubric.unknowns: Actual directory/files and behavior with missing arguments depend on supplied input; no recursive traversal is present.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim reading log contents, deleting files, recursive search or counting errors.

rubric.purpose: Group imported CSV rows by Status and emit group names/counts as JSON output.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Reads a CSV at the Path parameter; emits JSON for selected Name/Count group properties to the pipeline.
rubric.dependencies: PowerShell Import-Csv, Group-Object, Select-Object and ConvertTo-Json.
rubric.evidence: Lines 2, 3, 5: The pipeline performs import, grouping, projection and JSON conversion in order.
rubric.unknowns: Actual statuses/counts are unknown; single versus multiple results can affect the JSON shape.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim it writes a .json file, returns every original row, or always emits an array regardless of group count.

rubric.purpose: Define a parser for a base-10 port string, returning an integer within 1..65535 or nil on handled failures.
rubric.inputs_outputs: Receives value, converts and range-checks it; returns the number or nil. No caller or network operation is present.
rubric.dependencies: Ruby core Integer conversion, Range and exception handling; no gem.
rubric.evidence: Lines 2, 3, 5, 6: Integer(value, 10), the inclusive range, and rescue define success and failure paths.
rubric.unknowns: Actual input is unknown; accepted number does not establish that a port is open or a service exists.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim network probing, acceptance of zero/65536 or that all invalid input raises out of the function.

rubric.purpose: Create a temporary directory, write/read a marker within it, then leave the context so normal cleanup occurs.
rubric.inputs_outputs: No external input is shown; temporarily writes ready.txt, prints ready, then prints a closure message.
rubric.evidence: Lines 4, 6, 7, 8: The with context controls lifetime; write_text/read_text operate inside it; the final print is outside.
rubric.unknowns: Actual temporary path and exceptional filesystem outcomes are unknown; results are predictions from code inspection.
rubric.must_not_claim: Do not claim ready.txt is intentionally retained after normal completion or that the evaluator executed these file operations.
